newsitem.title: USA: US Senate bill proposes ending corporate loophole.
newsitem.headline: US Senate bill proposes ending corporate loophole.

text.p: A bill to be considered by the Senate Finance Committee this week offering sweeping tax reform would close one corporate tax loophole involving spinoffs as a way to offset tax cuts in the bill, according to papers released by the committee on Tuesday.
The bill would eliminate a popular technique used in mergers and acquisitions to get around taxes known as a "Morris Trust."

The bill, introduced by committee Chairman William Roth, Republican from Delaware, estimates that ending the Morris Trust provision would put $1.5 billion in the federal government coffers over the next five years.

A measure passed last week by the House Ways and Means Committee also would put an end to the tax loophole. House lawmakers say cutting the Morris Trust provision would put more than $1.6 billion over five years in the government's hands.

However, some members of the House panel said the revenue-raising measure may reach too far and expect to narrow that cut when both House and Senate lawmakers reconcile the differences in their two tax bills.
The Senate bill did not propose phasing out the corporate alternative minimum tax, a provision that was extended to small businesses in the House bill.
